::: {.why}
Example-based tests check the cases you thought of, and invariants check the ones you did not, which is the difference between a suite that passes and a suite that protects you.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- State five invariants your engine must satisfy for any strategy and any data, and assert them.
- Find at least one input on which an invariant fails, and either fix the engine or document the limitation.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [35 min]{.task-min} Write the invariants as tests run over randomised strategies and randomised data: the accounting identity, cash never negative beyond the allowed margin, position changes always explained by a fill, no fill outside the session's price range, and costs always non-negative. Run each over many random inputs rather than one.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Push until something breaks: feed the engine a session with zero volume, a price of zero, a missing bar mid-series, and a strategy that orders more than exists. Each should either be handled or fail loudly. A silent pass on any of them is a bug waiting for phase 10.
:::
:::

::: {.checkpoint}
Name an invariant your engine satisfies for every possible strategy, and say what bug it would catch.
:::
